stories.headline: METR and Epoch AI Show AI Agents Can Autonomously Complete Weeks-Long Coding Tasks

key_facts.fact: MirrorCode is a benchmark co-developed by METR and Epoch AI of long-horizon coding tasks derived from real software applications, testing AI ability to reimplement CLI programs without access to source code.
key_facts.excerpt: We present early results from MirrorCode, a benchmark (co-developed with METR) of long-horizon coding tasks derived from real software applications.

key_facts.fact: Claude Opus 4.6 successfully reimplemented gotree, a bioinformatics toolkit with ~16,000 lines of Go and 40+ commands, a task estimated to take a human engineer 2–17 weeks without AI assistance.
key_facts.excerpt: Claude Opus 4.6 successfully reimplemented gotree — a bioinformatics toolkit with ~16,000 lines of Go and 40+ commands. We guess this same task would take a human engineer without AI assistance 2–17 weeks.

key_facts.fact: The benchmark includes more than 20 target programs spanning Unix utilities, data serialization, bioinformatics, interpreters, static analysis, cryptography, and compression.
key_facts.excerpt: The full MirrorCode benchmark includes more than 20 target programs spanning different areas of computing: Unix utilities, data serialization and query tools, bioinformatics, interpreters, static analysis, cryptography, and compression.

key_facts.fact: The researchers observed continued gains from inference scaling on larger projects, suggesting bigger tasks may be solvable given enough tokens.
key_facts.excerpt: We see continued gains from inference scaling on larger projects, suggesting they may be solvable given enough tokens.

key_facts.fact: AI agents are given execute-only access to the original program and visible test cases but no source code, requiring them to make architectural design decisions autonomously.
key_facts.excerpt: The AI agent is given execute-only access to the original program and a set of visible test cases, but does not have access to the original source code. This means that the AI needs to make challenging decisions about how to design its solution.

sources.title: Evidence that AI can already do some weeks-long coding tasks

stories.headline: CoreWeave Lands Multi-Year Cloud Deal With Anthropic; Shares Surge Over 13%

key_facts.fact: CoreWeave struck a multi-year agreement with Anthropic to supply cloud computing capacity for Claude AI model workloads, with financial terms undisclosed.
key_facts.excerpt: Cloud infrastructure firm CoreWeave said it has struck a deal with Anthropic to supply the AI startup with cloud computing capacity, sending its shares up more than 13% on Friday.

key_facts.fact: CoreWeave shares surged more than 13% on Friday following the announcement, trading at $102.73.
key_facts.excerpt: Shares of CoreWeave surged more than 12% on Friday and are trading at $102.73 at the time of writing.

key_facts.fact: CoreWeave now serves nine of the ten major developers of large language models, having previously signed an $11.9B deal with OpenAI and an expanded $21B deal with Meta.
key_facts.excerpt: CoreWeave struck an $11.9 billion deal with OpenAI last year, a $6.3 billion initial order with Nvidia in September and an expanded $21 billion deal with Meta on Thursday.

key_facts.fact: The deal helps CoreWeave diversify revenue beyond Microsoft, which accounted for about 67% of its revenue last year.
key_facts.excerpt: The deal with Anthropic would also help CoreWeave diversify its revenue streams further - Microsoft accounted for about 67% of its revenue last year.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic has been rushing to secure more capacity, having also signed a deal with Broadcom and Google for AI capacity and exploring its own chip design.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic has been rushing to secure more capacity. Earlier this week, it signed a deal with Broadcom and Google for AI capacity, while Reuters exclusively reported on Thursday that Anthropic was exploring the possibility of designing its own chips.

stories.headline: Three OpenAI Stargate Infrastructure Leaders Leave to Join Meta

key_facts.fact: Peter Hoeschele, who played a critical role in OpenAI's Stargate initiative as VP of Industrial Compute, is joining Meta along with Shamez Hemani (computing strategy) and Anuj Saharan (computing organization leader).
key_facts.excerpt: Peter Hoeschele, who played a critical role in OpenAI's Stargate initiative, is one of the new hires. He'll be joined by Shamez Hemani, who worked on computing strategy and business development, and Anuj Saharan, another leader in the computing organization.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI hired former Intel Corp. executive Sachin Katti in November to lead its industrial compute efforts and does not plan to directly replace Hoeschele's role.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI didn't immediately respond to a request for comment, but previously said that the company was grateful for the contributions of the three employees and remains focused on hiring talent for its infrastructure plans. The company hired former Intel Corp. executive Sachin Katti in November to lead its industrial compute efforts.

key_facts.fact: Meta projected up to $135 billion in capital expenditures for 2026, with a focus on AI infrastructure projects, and Zuckerberg has pledged hundreds of billions more by end of decade.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta projected as much as $135 billion in capital expenditures, with a focus on AI infrastructure projects. Before the end of the decade, Zuckerberg has promised to spend hundreds of billions more on AI infrastructure projects.

key_facts.fact: Stargate was announced at the White House as a $500 billion venture between OpenAI, Oracle, and SoftBank; OpenAI also paused its Stargate UK project and abandoned an expansion at Abilene, Texas.
key_facts.excerpt: Stargate, meanwhile, was announced last year at the White House as a $500 billion venture between OpenAI, Oracle Corp. and SoftBank Group Corp. OpenAI said Thursday that it's pausing its Stargate artificial intelligence infrastructure project in the UK.

key_facts.fact: Hoeschele helped lead the Abilene, Texas data center site; he joined OpenAI in April 2019 and rose from Strategic Finance & Operations to VP of Industrial Compute.
key_facts.excerpt: Peter Hoeschele has left OpenAI, according to reports. He was one of the executives tied to the company's early Stargate data center initiative.

stories.headline: Ramp Data: Anthropic's US Business Adoption Jumps to 30.6%, Closing Gap With OpenAI

key_facts.fact: 30.6% of US businesses paid for Anthropic's tools in March, up from 24.4% in February — a 6.2 percentage point jump in one month.
key_facts.excerpt: Ramp data: 30.6% of US businesses paid for Anthropic's tools in March, up from 24.4% in February; OpenAI's US business adoption remained nearly flat MoM at ~35%

key_facts.fact: OpenAI's US business adoption remained nearly flat month-over-month at approximately 35%.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI's US business adoption remained nearly flat MoM at ~35%

key_facts.fact: Anthropic went from capturing roughly 10% of combined OpenAI-plus-Anthropic business subscription spend in early 2025 to commanding over 65% by February 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic went from capturing roughly 10% of combined OpenAI-plus-Anthropic business subscription spend in early 2025 to commanding over 65% by February 2026.

key_facts.fact: Sectors with the deepest AI adoption — Information, Finance, Professional Services — show the widest Anthropic lead over OpenAI.
key_facts.excerpt: The Information sector stands apart. It records the highest paid AI subscription rates of any industry in the Ramp dataset — and Anthropic's lead there is the widest in the chart. Finance and Professional Services follow a similar script.

key_facts.fact: The divergence is driven by strong interest in Claude Code products; Anthropic's annualized revenue surpassed $30 billion, with 80% from business customers.
key_facts.excerpt: the company crossed a $30 billion annualized run rate in early 2026, up from roughly $9 billion at the end of 2025, with 80% of revenue coming from business customers.

stories.headline: Alibaba Revealed Behind HappyHorse-1.0, Top-Ranked AI Video Generation Model

key_facts.fact: Alibaba confirmed it created HappyHorse-1.0, an anonymous AI video model that topped blind-test rankings on Artificial Analysis for both text-to-video and image-to-video generation.
key_facts.excerpt: HappyHorse-1.0, which appeared on the benchmarking platform Artificial Analysis around April 7, without identifying its affiliations, climbed to the top of blind-test rankings for both text-to-video and image-to-video generation.

key_facts.fact: The model was developed by Alibaba's ATH AI Innovation Unit and is still under development; the developers revealed the connection Friday via a newly created X account.
key_facts.excerpt: The developers revealed in a newly created X account Friday that HappyHorse was part of Alibaba's ATH AI Innovation Unit and that the project was still under development. Alibaba confirmed to CNBC that the post was genuine.

key_facts.fact: Alibaba's Hong Kong-listed shares closed 2.12% higher Friday after the reveal, following a 6.75% rise Wednesday amid speculation about the model's origin.
key_facts.excerpt: The Hong Kong-listed shares of Alibaba closed 2.12% higher Friday after news of its involvement. Its stock rose 6.75% on Wednesday.

key_facts.fact: The reveal comes as OpenAI recently discontinued its Sora video generation app and ByteDance paused Seedance 2.0 over copyright disputes with Hollywood studios.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI recently discontinued its Sora video generation app and platform, citing a strategic shift to focus on coding tools, corporate clients and AGI development amid high compute costs. ByteDance was recently forced to pause the rollout of its viral Seedance 2.0 following copyright disputes with major Hollywood studios.

sources.title: Alibaba revealed as creator of AI video generation model 'HappyHorse-1.0'

stories.headline: OpenAI Pauses Stargate UK Data Center Project Over Energy Costs and Regulation

key_facts.fact: OpenAI has paused its Stargate UK data center project in north-east England, citing rising energy costs and regulatory uncertainty as key barriers.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI has pressed pause on its Stargate UK data center project over rising energy costs and regulatory uncertainty in the country.

key_facts.fact: The project was part of a wider £31 billion UK tech investment package announced in September 2025, in partnership with Nvidia and Nscale, with plans to deploy up to 8,000 GPUs in Q1 2026 scaling to 31,000.
key_facts.excerpt: The project, in partnership with Nvidia and Nscale, was scheduled to 'explore offtake up to 8,000 GPUs in Q1 2026 with the potential to scale to 31,000 GPUs over time.'

key_facts.fact: OpenAI said it would only move forward 'when the right conditions such as regulation and the cost of energy enable long-term infrastructure investment,' citing copyright rules as a specific concern.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI 'continues to explore Stargate UK,' but will only move forward 'when the right conditions such as regulation and the cost of energy enable long-term infrastructure investment'. The company added that predictable frameworks, including rules around copyright, are central to its investment considerations.

key_facts.fact: The UK government recently withdrew proposals that would have permitted AI developers to use copyrighted material unless rights holders opted out, drawing tech sector criticism.
key_facts.excerpt: The UK government recently withdrew proposals that would have permitted AI developers to use copyrighted material unless rights holders opted out, drawing criticism from the technology sector.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI also decided not to lease an expansion to its Abilene, Texas Stargate site; the pause comes as the company reins in spending ahead of a planned public listing.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI said Thursday that it's pausing its Stargate artificial intelligence infrastructure project in the UK as it reins in ambitious spending plans ahead of a highly anticipated public listing. The company, along with Oracle, also decided not to lease an expansion to the site in Abilene.

sources.title: OpenAI just put the Stargate UK project on pause due to energy costs and regulations
